summary.answer: Applying g3's tombstone contract (PRIOR-MAPPINGS.json 27784-27838) and f2's dispatcher state graph ABSENT->ACTIVE->TOMBSTONE->purge with instant/all-clear/assert-abort arms (PRIOR-MAPPINGS.json 30049-30051) to only the newly identified scene/watcher teardown path. THE WATCHER TRIGGERED CALL: when the cscene::play 4484 notify completes its wait (callbacks_shared.gsc 188), the watcher runs remove_callback(event, func, self) (189) which is the 3-argument wrapper (196-199) delegating to function_3f5f097e( level, event, func, obj, instant-undefined ) (214+). Concrete differences against the generic routes: (1) TABLE = level ALWAYS: line 198 passes literal level, so the watcher route can never touch registrations stored on a non-level entity table (function_d8abfc3d self-table route 122-125; csc add_entity_callback csc 135-156 which additionally spawns no watcher); f2's R1 note (remove_callback always targets level table) is retained. (2) INSTANT = NEVER PASSED: the watcher route cannot trigger instant purge (236-240); the instant shape belongs only to third-party callers (killcam_shared.gsc 469-470: instant self-table removal function_52ac9652 with instant=1 then re-add). Therefore the scene teardown path leaves its tombstone physically in the list. (3) IDENTITY CONDITIONS: an affected entry must be isarray (244) with func_group[0] == func (loose) AND func_group[1] === obj (strict triple, 246); only the FIRST match is tombstoned (break 254). (4) STATE OUTCOMES per f2 graph: ACTIVE (registered 163, deduped 152-161) -> TOMBSTONE (slot = 0, 253) -> invisible to dispatch (non-array skip 66-69) and to dedup (isarray gate 154), so re-registration after a tombstone creates a second live entry beside it; physical purge ONLY at the next dispatch of that event on that table (105 arrayremovevalue(ent._callbacks[event], 0, 0)) or via an instant call (238). (5) RETAINED vs TOUCHED inside the scene teardown: same func/different obj retained; same event/different func retained; entries beyond the first match retained (break); self-table registrations unreachable; already-tombstoned entries skipped. (6) NEW ORDERING CAUTION, CONDITIONAL INFERENCE, NOT ASSERTED: source order at the tombstone site is `obj notify( watchkey )` (250) BEFORE the tombstone write (253), and this code executes inside the watcher's OWN resumed thread, which armed endon(watchkey) at 187; if native endon cancellation kills the executing thread at that notify (the same mechanism the prior S1 record used for the death arm - ordinary thread-wide endon would cancel it on death, unit-context/0002.json 351), the tombstone write could be skipped and the entry left ACTIVE; g3 and f2 recorded only the tombstone-kill shape. Both readings are bounded by the same retained native fact (g3 A.4 / f2 N4); neither is asserted. (7) CSC MIRROR DIFFERENCE: csc remove_callback (csc 198-214) physically removes via arrayremoveindex( level._callbacks[event], index, 0 ) under two asserts (200-201) - no tombstone on the client; csc function_52ac9652 (172-192) same arrayremoveindex shape on self tables; the func-equals / obj-triple identity conditions are VM-common. (8) Builtin contracts for arrayremovevalue/arrayremoveindex (x,0,0) remain g3 unknown 3 and are not asserted here. Required identity conditions for the scene teardown route to affect anything: registration made via the level-table route with obj exactly equal (strict) to the notified cscene instance and a still-alive watcher; obj=undefined registrations (wz block) have no watcher and are untouched.
summary.behavior: Scene/watcher teardown argument, table and instant facts: caller remove_callback_on_death 189 (3-arg, instant absent) -> remove_callback 196-199 (literal level) -> function_3f5f097e 214-258: no all-clear (individual func), no instant purge, foreach loop with isarray/loose-func/strict-obj conditions 244-246, obj notify key 250 then tombstone 253 then break; deferred purge only via next dispatch (dispatcher 105) or a foreign instant call 238; tombstones invisible to dispatch 66-69 and dedup 154. Entity-table (self-table) registrations unreachable by this route; killcam-style instant route (killcam_shared.gsc 469-470) is the only purge-at-rest shape in corpus. Conditional ordering caution on notify-before-tombstone recorded as inference, not asserted. csc mirror: arrayremoveindex physical removal under asserts (csc 198-214).
